The Mo Ibrahim Foundation is accepting applications for its 2027 Ibrahim Leadership Fellowships, a professional development programme designed for emerging African leaders with relevant work experience.

The fellowships provide selected professionals with first-hand experience of leadership, policy development and institutional decision-making at major African and international organisations.

Three fellows will be selected for 12-month placements at the African Development Bank Group, the United Nations Economic Commission for Africa and the International Trade Centre.

**Fellowship Benefits**

Successful fellows will receive:

US$100,000 stipend for the fellowship.

Twelve months of professional experience within a host institution.

Direct mentorship from senior institutional leaders.

Exposure to policy research, institutional leadership and decision-making.

Opportunities to build professional networks across Africa and internationally.

Membership of the Mo Ibrahim Foundation's Now Generation Network after completing the fellowship.

**Fellowship Host Institutions**

***The three placements are:***

***1. African Development Bank Group (AfDB)***

Location: Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire.

Fellows gain exposure to development finance, economic development and policy work within the African Development Bank Group.

***2. United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (ECA)***

Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

The placement offers experience related to African economic and social development, regional policy and institutional work.

***3. International Trade Centre (ITC)***

Location: Geneva, Switzerland.

The placement provides exposure to international trade, inclusive development and policy initiatives.

Applicants should consult the relevant host institution's application information because additional requirements and procedures may differ.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Applicants must:

Be nationals of an African country.

Hold a master's degree.

Have at least seven years of relevant professional experience.

Be under 40 years old, or under 45 for women with children.

Meet any additional requirements specified by the host institution.


**Programme Duration:**

12 months.

Each fellow works within the executive office of the selected host institution and contributes to research, policy work and institutional activities.

**How to Apply**

Applications are handled through the relevant host institutions. Applicants should review the requirements for their preferred placement and submit their applications through the corresponding official portal.

***African Development Bank Group***: https://www.afdb.org/

***International Trade Centre:*** https://careers.un.org/

***United Nations Economic Commission for Africa***: https://www.uneca.org/

The Mo Ibrahim Foundation's official fellowship page provides links to the host institutions' application information.

**Official fellowship details:**
https://mo.ibrahim.foundation/fellowships

**2027 fellowship announcement:**
https://mo.ibrahim.foundation/news/2026/applications-open-2027-ibrahim-leadership-fellowships

**Application Deadline**

20 November 2026.


**Important information:**


Applicants should check the relevant host institution's application instructions to confirm the applicable deadline and submission requirements.

The Fegho Umunubo Foundation has opened the second edition of its Grassroots Creative Business Support Initiative, known as GCBSI 2.0. The programme supports creative entrepreneurs and businesses in Nigeria through financial grants, business training and practical assistance aimed at strengthening operations and helping businesses reach more customers.

**What Selected Businesses Receive**

The initiative combines funding with business development support. Successful applicants can receive:

A business grant of ₦1 million to ₦1.5 million.
Training in areas such as marketing, bookkeeping, pricing and financial literacy.
Practical guidance to improve business operations, attract customers and build a more sustainable enterprise.

The programme is designed for creative businesses that need support to develop their services, improve how they operate and grow their customer base.

**Eligible Business Sectors**

The initiative is open to creative entrepreneurs and businesses in Nigeria. Sectors identified in published programme information include:

Media, film and entertainment.
Fashion, clothing, textiles and accessories.
Handmade products, arts and crafts.
Furniture, interior design and creative design.
Beauty and personal styling.
Photography, videography, printing and visual branding.
Food production, baking and creative confectionery.
Home fragrance businesses.


**How to Apply**

The application process includes preparing a short video introducing the business and explaining why financial support is needed. Applicants are instructed to share the one-minute video on Instagram using the hashtag #GCBSI and access the application form through the foundation's official social media channels.

The application form requests business and contact details, including the business name, CAC registration number, state of operation and how long the business has been running. Applicants should have this information ready before beginning.

**Application deadline:** 1 November 2026

**Official website**: https://www.feghoumunubofoundation.com/

**Application form**: https://forms.gle/b4CzNfGescrDhWho7

**Important information:**

Applicants should confirm the complete terms and conditions on the official application channel before submitting their details.

The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) has opened applications for its Blue Economy Accelerator Programme and National Innovation Hackathon. The initiative is designed to help young innovators develop practical solutions for Nigeria's maritime and blue economy, connecting promising ideas with opportunities for mentorship, business development and industry engagement.

The programme focuses on innovations that can strengthen the maritime sector, improve marine resource management and support new businesses across the blue economy.

**Who Can Apply?**

The programme's official announcement identifies young innovators aged 18 to 28 as the target applicants.

It is relevant to people developing solutions in areas such as:

1. Maritime technology and logistics.
2. Port operations and digitalisation.
3. Maritime safety and security.
4. Green shipping and vessel decarbonisation.
5. Marine waste management.
6. Aquaculture and sustainable fisheries.
7. Coastal protection and marine conservation.
8. Marine tourism and biotechnology.

Applicants should be able to explain the problem their idea addresses, how their proposed solution works and the potential benefit to Nigeria's maritime or marine economy.


 **Programme Stages and Timeline**

The programme is structured around several stages:

Applications open: 5 October 2026.
Application deadline: 13 November 2026.
Evaluation and due diligence: 16 November–2 December 2026.
National Innovation Hackathon: 8–10 December 2026.
Accelerator programme: First quarter of 2027.
National Demo Day: Second quarter of 2027.

Successful participants will progress through the relevant stages of the programme. The 12-week accelerator is intended to help selected innovators strengthen their solutions and prepare their ventures for further development. At Demo Day, participating ventures will have an opportunity to showcase their work to investors, industry stakeholders and potential partners.

The programme is not simply a general-purpose cash grant: its main focus is innovation development, acceleration and access to relevant industry networks.

**How to Apply**

Applications are handled through the NIMASA Blue Economy Accelerator Programme portal.

**Official application portal:**

https://nbeap.nimasa.gov.ng/programme

Application deadline: 13 November 2026


**Important information:**


The opportunity is particularly relevant to young Nigerians whose projects address real challenges in maritime transport, ports, fisheries, coastal communities or marine technology.

The #MyLittleBigThing Africa Student Innovation Challenge is accepting applications for its 2026/2027 edition, inviting young African innovators to turn sustainability ideas into practical ventures.

Organised by MK-Africa, the challenge supports innovators working on solutions connected to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Participants can develop their ideas, access learning resources and mentorship, and work towards building ventures with real-world impact.

Despite its student-focused name, the official call is open to African innovators aged 18–35; applicants should consult the rules to determine how their particular venture fits the challenge.

**Eligibility Requirements**

*Applicants must:*

Be between 18 and 35 years old.

Be based in Africa.

Have an innovation or venture addressing a relevant sustainability or development challenge.

Be prepared to explain their idea, its target beneficiaries and its potential impact.

Applicants do not need to have a formally registered business to apply.

**Application fee:** Free.

**Challenge Tracks**

Applicants must select the track that best matches the main problem their innovation addresses.

*1. Digital and Economic Inclusion*

For innovations involving financial technology, digital literacy, market access, connectivity and tools that help underserved groups participate in the economy.

*2. AgriTech and Circular Economy*

For solutions involving agriculture, food systems, waste-to-value initiatives, climate-resilient production and more sustainable use of resources.

*3. Empowering Women through Innovation*

For women-led ventures and innovations addressing issues such as maternal and reproductive healthcare, women's safety, care work and financial inclusion.

*4. Transparency and Governance Technology*

For innovations involving civic technology, public accountability, anti-corruption tools, data privacy and citizen participation in governance.

**Benefits**

Participants can access opportunities to:

Develop their ideas into practical ventures.

Take part in self-paced learning on the SDGs, venture ethics and circular business models.

Connect with a community of innovators.

Receive mentorship and venture-development support through the programme's stages.

Work towards building and testing a prototype.

Showcase selected innovations at the programme's Innovation Demo Day at Strathmore University in April 2027.

Participation does not guarantee that every applicant will reach the final demo day or receive investment.

The programme also offers an optional verified certificate for its self-paced course at a reported cost of US$20. This is separate from the free challenge application and is not compulsory for applying.

**Application Requirements**

The official application requests information about the founder, venture, team, development stage and selected thematic track.

Applicants should also prepare:

A short essay of approximately 200 words.

A short video pitch explaining the innovation.

Details about the problem, proposed solution and intended impact.

Consult the online application for the precise submission requirements.

**How to Apply**

Visit the official #MyLittleBigThing website.

Review the four challenge tracks.

Choose the track that best fits your innovation.

Prepare your founder and venture information, short essay and video pitch.

Complete and submit the online application.

**Application link:**
https://www.mylittlebigthing.com/

**Details of the 2026/2027 challenge:**
https://www.mylittlebigthing.com/2026-2027

**Application Deadline**

30 November 2026.


Official website: https://www.mylittlebigthing.com/

MIT Solve is inviting innovators worldwide to submit technology-based solutions for its 2027 Global Health Challenge. The challenge seeks practical innovations that can make healthcare more accessible, affordable and equitable, particularly for underserved communities.

The initiative is run by MIT Solve, an innovation programme that connects technology-driven solutions to global challenges with funding opportunities, mentorship and a network of partners.

Nigerian innovators, entrepreneurs, researchers and teams developing solutions to healthcare problems can apply.

**Challenge Focus**

The 2027 Global Health Challenge is seeking solutions that use technology to improve access to quality healthcare.

**Priority areas include:**

Strengthening continuity of care during disease outbreaks, climate emergencies, conflicts and funding disruptions.

Improving the prevention and management of noncommunicable diseases and mental health conditions.

Expanding access to quality primary healthcare for underserved communities.

Supporting frontline healthcare workers and reducing barriers related to cost, distance and administrative processes.

Solutions may use software, artificial intelligence, mobile technology, data systems, robotics or other appropriate technologies.

**Benefits**

Teams selected for the MIT Solve Global Health Challenge may receive:

At least US$25,000 in prize funding through the Collegium Prize for selected Global Health Solver teams.

A standard US$10,000 MIT Solve Solver Award.

Access to additional prize opportunities, subject to their individual eligibility and selection criteria.

A nine-month support programme involving workshops, leadership coaching and monitoring and evaluation support.

Access to a network of innovators, industry leaders and potential partners.

Opportunities for media exposure, networking and further funding.

Additional awards may be available to eligible solutions. Funding is competitive and is not guaranteed to every applicant.

**Eligibility Requirements**

MIT Solve encourages applications from innovators of different backgrounds and locations.

Applicants should have a technology-driven solution that:

Addresses a clearly defined global health problem.

Demonstrates an innovative and practical approach.

Has a credible plan for implementation and measurable impact.

Is designed with the needs of affected communities in mind.

Has potential for financial sustainability and expansion.

Solutions may be at different stages of development, including prototype, pilot, growth and scale. However, concept-stage ideas without a functioning prototype are generally considered only under the Indigenous Communities Fellowship, rather than this Global Health Challenge.


**How to Apply**

Visit the official MIT Solve 2027 Global Health Challenge page.

Review the challenge priorities, eligibility criteria and judging process.

Prepare information about the healthcare problem, your solution, the technology involved, its impact and implementation plan.

Explain how the solution can reach underserved communities and expand sustainably.

Submit the application through the official online portal.

**Application link:**
https://solve.mit.edu/challenges/2027-global-health-challenge

**Application Deadline**

6 November 2026 at 12:00 noon Eastern Time (ET).


**Important information:**
Applicants should begin early because the application requires detailed information about the solution and its potential impact.


**Official Website**

MIT Solve: https://solve.mit.edu/

The Awareness Africa Education Fund Scholarship 2026/2027 is advertised as a need-based financial assistance opportunity for Nigerian students preparing to begin their first undergraduate degree at a federal or state university.

The scholarship offers up to ₦500,000 towards school fees and compulsory university registration charges. It is intended to support students whose financial circumstances could prevent or significantly hinder their entry into higher education.

**Scholarship Benefits**

The advertised scholarship provides:

Financial assistance: Up to ₦500,000.

Covered expenses: School fees and compulsory university registration fees.

Target beneficiaries: Nigerian students commencing undergraduate studies in the 2026/2027 academic session.

The award is intended to help cover eligible university expenses. Accommodation, feeding allowances and monthly stipends have not been confirmed.

**Eligibility Requirements**

According to the published scholarship announcements, applicants should:

Be Nigerian citizens.

Be preparing to commence their first undergraduate studies.

Be entering a federal or state university in Nigeria for the 2026/2027 academic session.

Demonstrate academic commitment.

Have genuine financial need that may prevent or significantly hinder their ability to begin university.

The available announcements do not specify a minimum JAMB score, age limit or particular course of study.

**Who Is the Scholarship For?**

The opportunity is intended for prospective undergraduate students who have secured, or are preparing to complete, the requirements for entry into an eligible Nigerian university.

Students already enrolled in higher levels of undergraduate study and postgraduate applicants should not assume they qualify, as the published descriptions focus on students beginning their undergraduate education.

Private universities, polytechnics and colleges of education are not identified among the eligible institutions in the available announcements.

**How to Apply**

Interested candidates should complete the online application form using the link below.

Open the application form.

Read the instructions and eligibility requirements carefully.

Provide accurate personal, academic and university admission information.

Supply information about your financial circumstances as requested.

Upload any supporting documents required by the form.

Review your answers and submit the application.

**Application Form:**
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdjsitKhRAF3Mmw8JUUxzp9cKaCfju_J4PPl0usAV5mV43bNQ/viewform

Applicants should verify that the form corresponds to the Awareness Africa Education Fund Scholarship before submitting sensitive personal documents.

**Application Deadline**

31 October 2026


**Important Information**

The scholarship is advertised as providing up to ₦500,000, not a guaranteed payment of that amount to every applicant.

The number of beneficiaries, detailed selection process, complete document requirements and payment arrangements have not been independently confirmed through an accessible official source.

Applicants should not pay anyone who promises guaranteed selection and should verify requests for personal or financial information before responding.

One year of ISACA student membership.

An ISACA certificate review course from the available options.

Registration for an ISACA virtual conference.

Applicants must:

Be at least 18 years old.

Be enrolled in or accepted to an accredited college, university or technical training institute.

Be pursuing, or planning to pursue, a degree or advanced degree focused on cybersecurity.

International applicants must provide proof of enrolment as required by the application instructions.

Visit the official scholarship application page.

Create a free ISACA account or sign in to an existing account.

3 November 2026, at 11:59 p.m. US Central Time.

The TKA Solid Foundations has opened applications for its 2027 Nigerian College/University Scholarship Programme, offering 50 scholarships to students seeking admission into Nigerian public universities and polytechnics for the 2027 academic session.

The programme prioritises students from low-income families and aims to provide financial assistance to help them pursue higher education.

**Scholarship Benefits**

Selected beneficiaries may receive support covering the following:

Tuition and school fees.

Textbooks and stationery.

Bursary support.

The foundation has not specified the monetary value of the scholarship on the programme page.

**Eligibility Requirements**

Applicants must meet the following conditions:

Be seeking admission into a Nigerian public university or polytechnic for the 2027 academic session.

Have WAEC or equivalent examination results obtained between 2024 and 2027. Applicants awaiting their results may also apply.

Be preparing for the 2027 JAMB/UTME examination and admission process.

Be available to participate in the foundation's screening test in Lagos State.

Applicants from low-income families will receive priority consideration.

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements on the official application page before submitting their forms.

**Screening Test**

The foundation will conduct a screening test as part of the selection process.

Screening date: Saturday, March 13, 2027
Time: 9:00 a.m. (Nigeria time)
Location: Lagos State. The specific venue will be communicated to selected applicants by email.

Applicants should ensure they can attend the screening test before applying.

**Required Documents**

The online application page states that applicants do not need to create an account or upload files to submit their applications.

However, applicants must provide the requested personal information, educational details, WAEC or equivalent results, parent or guardian information, and intended university or polytechnic course choices.

Applicants awaiting their examination results are instructed to enter AR in the relevant subject fields. Where a subject is not applicable, the form instructs applicants to enter NA.

**How to Apply**

Interested and eligible applicants should follow these steps:

Visit the official scholarship application page.

Complete the online application form with accurate personal and educational information.

Provide the requested parent or guardian details.

Enter WAEC or equivalent results, or indicate awaiting results as instructed.

Provide four preferred university or polytechnic course choices.

Select the required subjects for the screening test.

Review the information provided and submit the application.

Keep the application reference number and monitor the email address provided for confirmation and subsequent updates.

**Appication link:** 

https://tkasolidfoundations.org/scholarships/2027-nigerian-scholarship

**Application Deadline**

December 20, 2026

Interested applicants are encouraged to apply before the deadline and confirm that they meet the programme's requirements.

**Important information:**

TKA Solid Foundations is a nonprofit organisation that provides financial, material and humanitarian assistance. Its areas of focus include education, empowerment, accommodation, social amenities and medical care.

The organisation's Nigerian operations are associated with the Timothy Kolawole Adebanjo Foundation.

The Elizabeth Alexander Creative Writing Award recognises outstanding creative writing through cash prizes, publication and a residency opportunity at Smith College in the United States.

The award is administered by Meridians: feminism, race, transnationalism, a journal based at Smith College.

**Benefits**

Each of the two annual winners receives:

$500 cash prize

Publication in Meridians

An opportunity to spend one week in residence at Smith College during the following fall or spring semester.

**Eligible Categories**

Applicants may submit work in the following categories:

Poetry

Fiction

Nonfiction

Play scripts

The award prioritises works engaging with feminism, race and transnationalism. Translations and manuscripts written in languages other than English are also encouraged.

Submission Requirements

All entries must be previously unpublished.

Only one submission per applicant is permitted.

Simultaneous submissions are not accepted.

Manuscripts must be submitted in PDF format.

The manuscript must not contain the applicant's name or contact information.

***Manuscript length:***

Poetry: 3–5 poems in one document.

Fiction and nonfiction: Maximum of 7,000 words.

Play scripts: Maximum of 5,000 words.

Manuscripts must include a title and follow the award's formatting guidelines.

**How to Apply**

Prepare your manuscript according to the requirements for your chosen category.

Save your submission as a PDF.

Remove identifying and contact information from the manuscript.

Complete the online application form and upload your work.

**Application Form:** https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeT9EHr6YBEmDtrSm0hLEeIczkdNfOdesLGDDaphbJGXWTH0A/viewform

**Official Website:** https://sites.smith.edu/meridians/awards/elizabeth-alexander-creative-writing-award/

Not confirmed.

The Paul Alaje Colloquium (TPAC) has announced its 2026 National Essay and Article Competition, inviting Nigerian students to explore how the country can strengthen its global reputation under the theme “The Brand Nigeria.”

The competition is open to students in secondary schools, undergraduate programmes and postgraduate programmes, with cash prizes for the top entry in each category.

**Competition Benefits**

The grand prizes are:

Postgraduate category: ₦1,000,000

Undergraduate category: ₦750,000

Secondary school category: ₦500,000

Essay Topics and Word Limits

***1. Postgraduate Category***

Topic: The Brand Nigeria, Beyond the Negative Narratives: Examining the Role of Governance, Innovation, Culture, and Citizens' Responsibility in Shaping Nigeria's Brand and Global Perception.

Word limit: 2,500–3,000 words.

***2. Undergraduate Category***

Topic: The Brand Nigeria: From Potential to Global Recognition — How Can Education, Entrepreneurship, Technology, and Creativity Help Strengthen Nigeria's Global Brand?

Word limit: 2,500–3,000 words.

***3. Secondary School Category***

Topic: The Brand Nigeria Starts With Me: How Can Good Character, Patriotism, Hard Work, and Innovation Help Build Nigeria's Image and Reputation?

Word limit: 1,000–1,500 words.

**Eligibility Requirements**

The competition has three categories for:

Secondary school students.

Undergraduate students.

Postgraduate students.

Applicants should select the category corresponding to their current educational level. The official announcement does not provide a specific age limit.

**Submission Requirements**

Applicants must ensure that their essays:

Are original and previously unpublished.

Follow the word limit for the selected category.

Are typed, double-spaced and formatted in 12-point Times New Roman.

Are submitted in PDF or Word format.

Include a cover page with the applicant's full name, institution, educational level or class, contact details and category.

Each participant may submit only one entry. Plagiarised or AI-generated submissions will be disqualified.

**How to Apply**

Visit the official competition page.

Applications are open for the January 2027 cohort of the ProMoat Capital Drawbridge Grant, which will award ₦1.5 million in total funding to two registered Nigerian businesses with paying customers.

The grant is designed to help existing businesses grow. Successful applicants will receive non-repayable funding without surrendering equity in their businesses.

**Grant Benefits**

Two businesses will receive the following awards:

First prize: ₦1,000,000.

Second prize: ₦500,000.

Total funding: ₦1,500,000.

The grants do not require repayment, and recipients will not give up any ownership stake in their businesses.

The funding can be used for business-growth expenses, including stock, equipment, tools, marketing and staff costs. Applicants must explain how they intend to use the money.

**Eligibility Requirements**

To qualify for the ProMoat Capital Drawbridge Grant, applicants must:

Operate a revenue-generating business in Nigeria.

Have a business registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC), either as a business name or a company.

Have paying customers.

Be at least 18 years old and authorised to represent the business.

Businesses from different sectors can apply. The programme does not require applicants to operate in the technology sector or have a long business history, provided their businesses are registered and have paying customers.

A dedicated business bank account is preferred but is not compulsory. However, grant payments can only be made into a bank account held in the business's name or the applicant's name.

**Application Process and Selection**

Applicants must complete the online application form and create a free account on ProMoat Capital's small-business platform to track their application.

A pitch deck or separate formal business plan document is not required for the initial application.

The selection process comprises the following stages:

***Application***: Submit the online form by the deadline.

***Initial review and interviews***: Applications will be reviewed, and shortlisted businesses will be contacted for interviews in December 2026.

***Final interviews:*** Final interviews are scheduled for early January 2027.

***Grant awards:*** The two successful businesses are expected to receive their grants by the end of January 2027.

Applicants should provide accurate information about their businesses, customers, revenue and intended use of the grant.

**Is the Grant Repayable?**

No. The Drawbridge Grant is a grant, not a loan or an equity investment. Recipients are not required to repay the funding or surrender ownership of their businesses.

ProMoat Capital may separately approach some applicants about potential investment opportunities. Any such discussions are optional and independent of the grant award.

**How to Apply**

The TEEEM Foundation is a programme that supports community-driven initiatives that promote education, youth development, healthcare, gender equality, entrepreneurship, economic opportunities and sustainable community development offering financial support to nonprofit and charitable organisations working to improve lives and strengthen communities.

Through this initiative, the foundation seeks to partner with organisations that understand the needs of their communities and can demonstrate strong leadership, responsible financial management and a clear plan for achieving measurable, lasting impact.


**Grant Benefits**

Successful applicants may receive funding under one of three grant categories:

- Community Grants: US$5,000 to US$10,000 for grassroots projects and local community initiatives.
- Growth Grants: US$10,000 to US$20,000 for organisations seeking to expand successful programmes and reach more beneficiaries.
- Transformational Grants: US$20,000 to US$30,000 for larger initiatives with the potential to deliver sustainable, long-term change.

Organisations requesting amounts outside these ranges may also be considered. Funding may be awarded in full or in part, depending on the foundation's assessment and available funding.

**Areas of Focus**

The programme supports projects in the following areas:

- Education and youth development: Initiatives that expand educational access, promote youth leadership and create development opportunities for young people.
- Health and essential needs: Projects addressing food security, basic needs, access to medical care and community health.
- Equality and empowerment: Programmes supporting underserved populations, women's empowerment and gender equity.
- Entrepreneurship and economic opportunity: Initiatives that develop skills, strengthen livelihoods and expand economic opportunities.
- Community infrastructure: Projects that improve the physical and social infrastructure communities need.
- Sustainable community development: Community-led initiatives with measurable outcomes and the potential to create lasting change.

The foundation expects funded organisations to demonstrate accountability through progress reports, financial updates and evidence of project impact.

**Who Can Apply?**

The grant is intended for nonprofit and charitable organisations developing sustainable, community-driven solutions.

Organisations interested in applying should demonstrate the following:

- They operate as an eligible nonprofit organisation, registered charity or other qualifying charitable institution.
- They have a clear understanding of the needs of the communities they serve.
- They can demonstrate strong leadership and responsible financial management.
- They develop solutions that involve community members in planning and implementation.
- Their proposed projects have measurable objectives and realistic expected outcomes.
- They can explain how their projects will remain sustainable beyond the grant period.
- Their activities align with the foundation's focus on empathy, equality, entrepreneurship, service and community impact.
- They have the organisational capacity to implement and manage the proposed project successfully.

**Documents Required**

Applicants should consult the official application form for the complete list of mandatory supporting documents.

The published application information and supporting programme materials identify the following documents as relevant to the application process:

- Completed TEEEM Foundation Community Impact Grant Application.
- Proof of nonprofit or charitable status, such as an IRS determination letter or equivalent registration documentation.
- Recent financial statements.
- Current organisational budget.
- Detailed project budget explaining how the requested funds will be used.
- List of the organisation's board of directors.
- Annual report, where available.
- Supporting materials demonstrating the organisation's work and community impact.

Additional materials, such as a strategic plan, letters of support, photographs and other evidence of impact, may strengthen an application where relevant.

Applicants should verify which documents are mandatory and which are optional in the official application before submitting their proposals.

**How to Apply**

Eligible nonprofit and charitable organisations can apply by following these steps:

1. Visit the official TEEEM Foundation website using the link provided below.
2. Open the Community Impact Grant Programme page.
3. Download the official grant application form.
4. Read the eligibility criteria, funding categories, reporting requirements and application instructions carefully.
5. Complete the application with accurate information about the organisation, the community need being addressed and the proposed project.
6. Prepare the required supporting documents, including evidence of charitable status, financial records, organisational information and a detailed project budget.
7. Explain the project's expected outcomes, how success will be measured and how the initiative will remain sustainable.
8. Combine the completed application and supporting documents into a single PDF file, as instructed by the foundation.
9. Email the complete application package to the designated contact before the application deadline.



The official Community Impact Grant Application can be accessed through the foundation's website.

**Application form:**
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1cGaV3q9cvYoMRotB88ZqCfaoankJHqI0/view?usp=sharing

**Official programme page:**
https://www.teeem.org/foundation

Applicants should read the complete application form before preparing their submissions.

Application Email

Completed applications and supporting documents should be submitted electronically, following the instructions in the official application form.

Contact person: Michelle Della Fortuna
Position: Vice President of Finance and Strategy
Email: michelle@teeem.org

Applicants should confirm the required submission procedure and any email-subject instructions in the application documents before sending their applications.

**Official Website**

The official programme page contains information about the funding categories, areas of focus, application process and reporting requirements.

**Application Deadline**

1 November 2026.


Interested organisations should submit their applications before the deadline and allow sufficient time to prepare the required supporting documents.


**Applications will be evaluated based on five principal considerations:**

- Mission alignment: How closely the proposed project aligns with the foundation's objectives and values.
- Organisational capacity: Whether the organisation has the leadership and resources required to implement the project.
- Community need: The importance of the problem the project seeks to address.
- Sustainability: Whether the proposed benefits can continue beyond the grant period.
- Anticipated impact: The project's potential to produce measurable and meaningful improvements in the community.

Submitting an application does not guarantee funding. The foundation may award the full amount requested or provide partial funding.

Successful organisations will also be expected to submit a mid-year progress report, a final impact report and financial updates detailing how the grant funds were used. They may be required to share photographs, stories, testimonials and other materials documenting project outcomes.

**Important Information**

The TEEEM Foundation Community Impact Grant is designed to support organisations delivering sustainable, community-driven solutions rather than individuals seeking personal financial assistance.

Nigerian nonprofit organisations and registered charities with relevant projects may consider applying, provided they satisfy the programme's eligibility and documentation requirements.

**Before applying, organisations should:**

- Confirm that their legal status satisfies the foundation's requirements.
- Ensure that the proposed project falls within an eligible funding area.
- Prepare a realistic and detailed project budget.
- Establish measurable outcomes and a practical plan for evaluating impact.
- Explain how the project will remain sustainable after the funding period.
- Review the complete application form for additional conditions and reporting obligations.

The foundation expects funded organisations to maintain financial accountability and provide progress reports and evidence of project impact.

**Application deadline:** 1 November 2026.

The initiative supports newly admitted university students who demonstrate academic ability, financial need and a commitment to serving their community.



**Scholarship Benefits:**
Successful applicants may receive:

- Annual scholarship: ₦500,000 per year for the official duration of their university course.
- First Class incentive: ₦1,000,000 for eligible beneficiaries who graduate with First Class honours in a bachelor's degree.
- Mentorship: Access to mentors and leadership development opportunities.
- Community service: Opportunities to contribute to the development of Ukawu.

The initiative selects three new scholars annually, according to its published programme information.

**Who Can Apply?**

Applicants must:

- Be indigenes of Ukawu, Onicha LGA, Ebonyi State.
- Come from a financially disadvantaged family.
- Be 25 years old or younger at the time of application.
- Have at least five credits in WAEC or NECO.
- Have written JAMB and met the qualifying admission cut-off.
- Have secured admission into a recognised Nigerian university.
- Be entering university for the first time and have never enrolled in another higher institution.
- Be unmarried at the time of application and throughout the scholarship period.
- Demonstrate good character and a commitment to community service.

Applicants must also ensure that their proposed course of study is among those approved by the initiative.

**Documents Required**

Applicants must prepare:

- WAEC or NECO result.
- JAMB result slip.
- University admission letter.
- Two passport photographs.
- Reference letter from a ward councillor or community leader.

Applicants should upload clear copies of the required documents when completing the online application.

1. Visit the official application page.
2. Complete the online application form with accurate information.
3. Upload the required documents.
4. Review and submit the application.
5. Download and complete the paper application and reference forms as instructed.
6. Submit the completed forms and photocopies of supporting documents to the appropriate community leader.

30 October 2026.

Applications undergo eligibility and document verification. Qualified applicants enter a village-based public raffle draw intended to ensure representation across Ukawu.

This scholarship is exclusively for eligible indigenes of Ukawu who have secured admission into a Nigerian university and meet the programme's academic, financial and other requirements.

The AfriSEED Foundation is an educational support programme designed to help academically promising Nigerian students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds overcome the financial barriers to university admission.

The initiative focuses on students who have completed secondary school or are approaching graduation but cannot afford the qualifying examinations required to enter a Nigerian university.

Through the programme, selected students receive financial assistance for examination fees, structured mentorship, academic and career guidance, and support in identifying and applying for undergraduate scholarships.

The Root Initiative is the foundation's flagship programme, with an annual intake of 15 students. Its goal is to help young people progress from secondary school towards higher education without financial hardship preventing them from taking the necessary admission examinations.

**Scholarship Benefits**

Successful applicants selected for the Root Initiative will receive the following support:

WAEC/WASSCE examination fees: Financial assistance to cover registration fees for the West African Senior School Certificate Examination.

JAMB/UTME examination fees: Support for registration for the Unified Tertiary Matriculation Examination.

Post-UTME examination fees: Assistance with institution-specific screening examination fees where applicable.

Structured mentorship: Two group mentorship sessions each semester and individual check-ins with a dedicated mentor every two months.

Academic and career guidance: Support to help participants navigate their educational journey and prepare for future opportunities.

Undergraduate scholarship guidance: Assistance with identifying and applying for scholarships and other educational funding opportunities.


Important: The Root Initiative is not a full university scholarship. The foundation states that university tuition fees, books, academic materials, stationery, and living expenses are not currently covered.

**Who Can Apply?**

To be considered for the 2026 Root Initiative, applicants should meet the following requirements:

They must be Nigerian nationals or legal residents.

They must have completed secondary school or be approaching graduation.

They must demonstrate genuine financial need and an inability to pay the required examination fees independently.

They must have strong academic performance supported by school records.

They must provide a recommendation from a teacher.

They must provide an additional recommendation from a parent, community leader, or religious leader.

They must demonstrate a clear intention to pursue university education.


The foundation reviews applications holistically, considering academic potential alongside financial need, character, and commitment to education.

Applicants should consult the official programme page and application form for any additional requirements.

**Documents Required**

The foundation's programme page specifies academic records and recommendations as part of its eligibility assessment but does not provide a complete, separate checklist of required documents.

Academic records demonstrating their educational performance.

A recommendation from a teacher.

Information explaining their financial circumstances and need for assistance.

Personal and contact information.

Details demonstrating their intention to pursue university education.


Applicants should check the online application form for the complete list of required documents and submit any additional materials requested by the foundation.

**How to Apply**

**About**

The National Youth Pension Literacy Essay Competition 2026 invites Nigerian students and young people serving in the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) to share their ideas on retirement planning, financial independence and the future of pensions in Nigeria.



The competition is part of National Pension Week 2026 and is designed to help young Nigerians understand why retirement planning matters, even at an early stage of life. Participants are encouraged to consider how personal financial decisions, public policies and new ideas can contribute to a better retirement experience for Nigerians.



**Essay topic**

"My Dream for a Great Retirement Experience in Nigeria"



Participants must write an original essay explaining their vision for a better retirement experience in Nigeria. Strong entries should demonstrate an understanding of pensions and financial security, identify existing challenges and propose practical ways to improve retirement outcomes.



**Who can apply**



The competition has two categories.



1. Category A: Secondary school students: This category is open to students currently enrolled in a recognised secondary school in Nigeria. The maximum essay length is 500 words.



1. Category B: Tertiary institution students and NYSC members. This category is open to students currently enrolled in recognised Nigerian universities, polytechnics and other eligible tertiary institutions, as well as serving NYSC members.The maximum essay length is 1,000 words.



***Applicants must enter the category that corresponds to their current educational or service status. Participants under 18 must provide parental or legal guardian consent.***



**Competition prizes**



* Category A winner: **1,000,000** **naira,** a laptop, a trophy and a certificate.



* Category B winner: **1,500,000** **naira**, a laptop, a trophy and a certificate.



The total cash prize pool is 2,500,000 naira. Outstanding entries may also receive national recognition during the National Pension Week gala ceremonies.



**Essay requirements**



* Your essay must address the official topic and be your original work.



* The essay must have a title and stay within the word limit for the relevant category. Entries must be submitted as PDF, DOCX or TXT files, with a maximum upload size of 10 MB.



* Participants should ensure that their essays are clearly organised, relevant to the topic and supported by sound reasoning. Where facts or quotations are used, sources should be acknowledged appropriately.



* The organisers may screen entries for plagiarism and request an oral explanation from shortlisted candidates to confirm authorship.



**Artificial intelligence and originality rules**



* The organisers require the essay to reflect the entrant's own ideas and writing. An essay substantially generated or rewritten by a generative AI system must not be submitted as the participant's own work.



* Standard spelling, grammar and reference tools may be used. Limited research assistance or brainstorming involving AI should be disclosed as required by the competition rules.



* Applicants should therefore develop their own arguments, write in their own voice and ensure that the submitted work genuinely represents their understanding of the topic.



**How entries will be judged**



For Category A, the judging criteria are:



1. Originality and creativity: 30 percent.



* Understanding of pensions and retirement planning: 25 percent.



* Relevance to the topic: 20 percent.



* Organisation and clarity: 15 percent.



* Grammar and writing quality: 10 percent.



For Category B, the judging criteria are:



* Research and understanding: 25 percent.



* Critical thinking: 25 percent.



* Practical recommendations: 20 percent.



* Innovation and originality: 15 percent.



* Structure and writing quality: 15 percent.



*Applicants should pay attention to the criteria for their category when planning and reviewing their essays.*



**Documents and information to prepare**



Before starting the application, prepare your completed essay, full name, email address, phone number and school or institution details.



You will also need your class or academic level and state of residence or institution details requested by the form. The registration form requests a student or institutional identifier where applicable, such as a matriculation number, student ID, admission number or NYSC call-up number.



Participants under 18 must provide their parent or guardian's name and contact information and complete the required consent process.



Shortlisted applicants may be asked to provide student identification, evidence of enrolment or NYSC status and additional information for verification.



**How to apply**

Visit the official National Pension Week essay competition page.



Select the appropriate category and provide your personal and school or institution information.



Enter your essay title and upload your completed essay in PDF, DOCX or TXT format. Ensure that the file is no larger than 10 MB.



Review the declarations, confirm that your information is accurate and submit your entry through the official platform.



Keep the submission confirmation and check your email for further communication from the organisers.

The Ruth Titilayo Educational Foundation (RTEF) is offering scholarships for the 2027 academic cycle to support students who face financial barriers to education. The Foundation works to make education more accessible to disadvantaged students by providing financial assistance at different stages of their academic journeys.

The 2027 scholarship application window is open from 1 October to 31 October 2026. Several categories are available, including secondary school, undergraduate, postgraduate, polytechnic, and technical and vocational scholarships. Applicants should select the category that matches their current educational level.

**Ruth Titilayo Undergraduate Scholarship 2027**

**Who can apply**

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

1. They must be domiciled in Nigeria.
2. They must be under 25 years old.
3. They must currently be a student or have been registered as a student within the last three years.
4. They must have a minimum GPA of 4.0 on a 5-point scale or its equivalent.
5. Students studying at federal and state universities in Nigeria are eligible. Final-year undergraduates may also apply.

**Scholarship benefits**

Successful applicants may receive a tuition allowance of up to 100,000 naira and a maintenance allowance of up to 20,000 naira. Additional assistance, such as internal travel costs related to a course, research or fieldwork expenses, may be awarded at the committee's discretion.

**Ruth Titilayo Postgraduate Scholarship 2027**

**Required documents**

Applicants should be prepared to provide their current academic results, two reference letters from their tutors, a personal statement and other supporting documents requested by the Foundation.

**About** 

The Osun State Indigenes Organization USA Chapter has announced its scholarship programme for the 2026/2027 fiscal year to support sons and daughters of Osun State who need financial assistance to pursue higher education.

The organisation is a nonprofit association of Osun State indigenes and supporters, primarily based in the United States. Through its charitable programmes, it supports education, healthcare, humanitarian assistance and community development in Osun State.

The scholarship is intended to help financially disadvantaged students continue their education by providing financial assistance towards their studies.

**Scholarship benefits**

Successful applicants will receive a scholarship or bursary award of 100,000 naira.

The scholarship funds will be paid directly to the school identified by the successful applicant after verification. Beneficiaries will be notified in writing.

The award is intended to help reduce the financial burden of higher education. Applicants should note that the published award is 100,000 naira and should not assume that it covers all educational expenses.

**Who can apply**

* To be eligible for the 2026/2027 scholarship, applicants must meet the following requirements.
* They must be indigenes of Osun State.
* They must have gained admission to a college or university.
* They must be enrolled or accepted as full-time students.
* They must demonstrate financial need.
* They must maintain good academic standing and show the self-discipline required to pursue their education successfully.
* The scholarship is intended for students who need financial assistance. Applicants should provide accurate information about their educational status and financial circumstances.

* A recommendation from a teacher who is familiar with the applicant's educational goals.

5. The most recent school transcript.

Applicants should ensure that the essay addresses the prescribed topic and that all three recommendations are obtained before submission.

**Essay requirements**

* The essay must be two pages long, typed and double-spaced. It should explain how the applicant intends to make a positive difference in their community.
* A strong essay should identify a genuine problem, explain why it matters and describe practical actions the applicant would take to address it. Applicants should use specific examples and explain how their education, skills or future plans could benefit their communities.
* The essay should reflect the applicant's own experiences and ideas rather than general statements about helping people.

- Nigerian students who are **newly admitted** into a Nigerian university and hold a valid admission
- Students from any of the 36 states or the FCT

## What you get

Tuition support. The announcement does **not** state an amount, so ask the scholarship team if you need clarity.

## Documents to prepare

- A valid means of identification
- Your university admission letter
- WAEC or NECO result
- JAMB result
- Birth certificate
- A cover letter

## How to apply

Use the **Apply now** button to open the online application form, fill it in accurately and upload your documents before **15 November 2026**. The application is free.

For questions about eligibility, the amount or the selection process, email iconscholarship@whiteavenuemail.com.

The Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at the University of Edinburgh funds postgraduate study for exceptional young Africans who have shown leadership, overcome barriers to education and want to make a positive impact, particularly on climate and sustainability.

## Important: new application process for 2027/28

Edinburgh changed the process this year:

- Applicants had to attend a **mandatory virtual information session held between 15 and 24 September 2026** to be considered
- Eligible attendees learn on **13 October 2026** whether they have been invited to apply
- Invited applicants complete a short first stage, then the **Scholarship Main Application, which closes on 19 November 2026 at 5:00 p.m. UK time**
- Do **not** apply for your degree programme first. The scholarship application comes first, and awardees (announced March 2027) are then invited to apply for their programme

If you did not attend an information session, check the official page to see whether any route is still open before you spend time on this.

## What it covers

- Full funding for a one-year on-campus master's degree or an online postgraduate diploma
- Participation in the wider Climate Leadership Programme, including online workshops, coaching and support

## Who can apply

- African applicants who will have completed an undergraduate degree by 19 November 2026
- Candidates who have faced significant barriers to education or early career opportunities
- Applicants who show leadership, community service and a commitment to creating positive impact
- Applicants who qualify academically for admission to one of the eligible Edinburgh programmes (generally a UK 2:1 equivalent or higher)

## How to apply

Read the full process and the list of eligible programmes on the official Edinburgh page using the **Apply now** button.

The Pro. Dr. Gabriel Olubunmi Fakeye (GOF) Scholarship & Bursary Award is offered by the Cherubim & Seraphim Movement Church, Surulere District Headquarters, Lagos. It supports dedicated church members in their undergraduate studies.

## Who can apply

- Indigent members of the Cherubim & Seraphim Movement Church, Surulere District and its branches
- Undergraduates at a Nigerian public tertiary institution
- For the **Scholarship Award**: a minimum CGPA of 3.5
- For the **Bursary Award**: a minimum CGPA of 3.0

## Awards

- **Scholarship:** ₦300,000 each for 2 beneficiaries
- **Bursary:** ₦100,000 each for 40 beneficiaries

## Documents to upload

- Admission letter
- Your latest academic result showing your current CGPA, signed by an authorised officer of your institution
- A recommendation letter from your Branch Leader. If you cannot get one, state the reason in the application
- A passport photograph

Result, admission and recommendation files can be PDF, DOC or DOCX. The photograph can be JPG, JPEG or PNG. Each file must be 5 MB or less.

## How the selection works

1. Create your profile, complete the form, upload your documents and submit
2. Documents are verified and screened
3. Shortlisted candidates take an examination and attend an interview
4. Approved awards are paid directly to the bank account you provide

## How to apply

Applications opened on 4 October 2026 and close on **4 December 2026**. Use the **Apply now** button to reach the official application portal.

The Bode Amao Foundation (BAF) Scholarship supports academically strong Nigerian undergraduates who cannot afford the cost of university education. Beneficiaries can keep the award throughout their course of study as long as they maintain the required academic standard.

## Who can apply

- Registered students of Nigerian universities who are **at least in 200 level** when they complete the form
- Applicants with strong academic performance (CGPA is an important factor)
- Students who can prove financial need. The university Registrar must certify that the applicant is indigent
- Open to Nigerians regardless of tribe, sex, religion or age

## What you get

- Full tuition support
- ₦100,000 stipend for each academic year
- Continued support for the rest of your course, subject to academic excellence

## Documents to prepare

- Completed application form and academic transcript
- Letters of recommendation from higher authorities
- University student ID card, plus a Local Government Area letter of identification
- Original medical certificate (including HIV test document)
- JAMB admission letter, university admission letter and course registration form

## How to apply

Download and print the application form from the foundation's official website using the **Apply now** button, fill it in, attach the documents above and get it attested by your university Registrar. Submit only one application. False information leads to automatic disqualification.

Completed forms can be sent by email to the addresses on the foundation's official page, or by post to: Bode Amao Foundation (BAF), P.O. Box 7088, Secretariat Post Office, Ibadan, Oyo State.

IELTS is not required.
posts.summary: Full tuition support plus a ₦100,000 annual stipend for academically strong but indigent Nigerian university students (200 level and above).

The African Organisation for Standardisation (ARSO) has opened entries for its 14th Continental Essay Competition. Students explore practical solutions that can strengthen trade between African countries.

## Essay theme

*Advancing Intra-African Trade through Conformity Assessment and Mutual Recognition Agreements (MRAs): Unlocking the Full Potential of the Cotton-to-Clothing Value Chain under the AfCFTA.*

## Who can apply

- Citizens or residents of a participating African country
- Undergraduate or postgraduate students at a recognised tertiary institution, in any discipline
- Applicants under 35 years old
- One original, unpublished entry per person

## Essay requirements

- 1,000 to 1,200 words (not counting references and author details), in English or French
- Century Gothic, size 12, double-spaced
- Submitted as a PDF or Word (.docx) file
- No plagiarism and no AI-generated content. Such entries are disqualified

## What to submit

- The completed ARSO registration form (download it from the official page)
- A copy of your student ID card or passport
- Your essay

Send these through your country's National Standards Body or the country-specific email listed on the official page. In Nigeria the national standards body is the Standards Organisation of Nigeria.

## Prizes

- 1st place: US$1,000, a certificate and travel sponsorship to the 33rd ARSO General Assembly
- 2nd place: US$800 and a certificate
- 3rd place: US$500 and a certificate
- National winners receive certificates and prizes from their national bodies

## Important dates

- **3 September 2026:** call for entries opened
- **23 April 2027:** last day for participating countries to send their selected entries to ARSO
- **July 2027:** continental winners announced

**Your national body will set an earlier cut-off than ARSO's.** Confirm it on the official page or with your national standards body, and do not wait until April.
